gaps.description: Limited longitudinal data on long-term technical debt accumulation from AI coding agents beyond 6-month windows
gaps.reasoning: Most studies cover 6-12 months; true technical debt impact may take years to manifest in production systems

gaps.description: Lack of standardized, widely-adopted benchmarks for evaluating security of AI-generated code in repository-level contexts
gaps.reasoning: Existing benchmarks (SWE-bench, HumanEval) focus on functional correctness; security evaluation remains ad hoc

gaps.description: Insufficient research on optimal human-AI collaboration patterns for senior developers in complex, mature codebases
gaps.reasoning: Most studies focus on junior developers or simple tasks; senior-specific workflows understudied

gaps.description: ROI measurement methodologies for enterprise AI coding agent deployments remain immature
gaps.reasoning: Vendors report productivity gains but independent ROI studies with controlled designs are rare

gaps.description: Governance frameworks for enterprise agent deployment (visibility, control, compliance) are nascent
gaps.reasoning: Gartner notes this as emerging challenge; few established best practices exist

gaps.description: Limited understanding of how prior AI tool exposure affects subsequent agent adoption and productivity
gaps.reasoning: AIDev study found front-loaded gains only in AI-naive settings; interaction effects need more research

gaps.description: Scarcity of research on multi-agent coordination failures and debugging strategies
gaps.reasoning: Multi-agent workflows are emerging; failure modes and recovery strategies are poorly documented

gaps.description: Developer mental model degradation from reduced code reading ('use it or lose it' effect)
gaps.reasoning: Anecdotal evidence exists; no longitudinal studies measuring codebase knowledge retention

credibility_assessment.methodology_note: Assessment based on 15 claims across 20+ sources. Tier 1 sources (academic papers, primary vendor docs) form the backbone of high-confidence claims. Market sizing and adoption figures (Tier 2) involve more projection uncertainty. Senior developer-specific insights are well-supported by Cornell/UCSD study but would benefit from replication.
